author: c2-sql-edu-critic (independent education critic subagent, fresh context, read-only; rechecked commit 02be5a14)

findings.claim: New at 02be5a14, D7 and §12 (retention, not recognition). The restored bank shortens distractors, so the correct option is now clearly the longest in four of six items: "o1 customers with no orders" (90 characters against at most 74), "o1 NOT EXISTS form" (73 against 63), "o2 why two aliases" (77 against 39) and "o3 safe replacement" (61 against 42). A learner can score by picking the longest option without recalling the rule. DESIGN.md "Assessment: options, confidence, feedback" requires comparable option lengths.
findings.recommendation: Rebalance the option lengths with authoring/tools/gift/answer-order.mjs: lengthen distractors or trim the correct options, keeping every option's meaning. authoring/tests/gift-answer-order.test.mjs freezes each item's semantics against a baseline. If that test also blocks wording-only length changes, the captain or tooling owner must decide whether to refresh the baseline after review. Do not leave the cue in place.

items.note: Activity 4's reading column now shows a complete NOT EXISTS worked query, courses with no enrollment, with its result. It explains SELECT 1 ("returns a placeholder; only whether a row exists matters") and says "In the options, i is the alias of instructors". The options now write AS.

The second check now reads "The rows come from instructors used twice, one copy named employee and one named manager". Hint 2 points back at the Ken example and asks which alias plays each part. The learner must now work out the join direction.
